To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the remaining forest is distributed in a very fragmented pattern, with most fragments being small and located near the edges of the forest; (2) the amount of forest remaining was higher than previously estimated, but the spatial distribution of the forest remains highly fragmented; (3) the amount of remaining forest and its spatial distribution varies considerably across the Atlantic Forest, and conservation strategies must be tailored to each sub region; and (4) conservation strategies must consider the spatial distribution of forest fragments, as
(i) the Brazilian Atlantic Forest still has a high degree of endemism, and (ii) it has lost 85% of its area.
8% of the original Atlantic Forest remains, but 32% of what remains is composed of small fragments, and 9% of it is protected by nature reserves.
